questions.question: A vector A lies in a plane. If the coordinate system is rotated by an angle of 30°, then the magnitude of the vector |A|:
questions.explanation:
The magnitude of a vector represents its length, which is a scalar quantity. Rotating the
coordinate system changes the components of the vector, but the magnitude remains
unchanged.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct representation of a null vector resulting from the cross product of a vector with itself?

options.D: Null vectors cannot be produced by cross products

questions.explanation:
The cross product of a vector with itself is always a null vector because the angle
between the two vectors is 0°, and sin 0° = 0.

questions.question: If the x-component of a vector is positive and the y-component is negative, the vector lies in the:
questions.explanation:
A positive x-component and a negative y-component place the vector in the fourth
quadrant.

questions.question: The projection of vector A in the direction of vector B is given by:
questions.explanation: The projection of vector A in the direction of vector B is equal to A cos θ.

questions.question: Two vectors act on a point. The magnitude of their resultant is maximum when the angle between them is:
questions.explanation:
The resultant of two vectors is maximum when the angle between them is 0°, meaning
both vectors act in the same direction.

questions.question: If |A · B| = |A × B|, the angle between vectors A and B is:
questions.explanation: If |A · B| = |A × B|, then cos θ = sin θ, which gives θ = 45°.

questions.question: The magnitude of the cross product of two parallel vectors A and B is:
questions.explanation:
For parallel vectors, the angle between them is 0°, therefore the cross product becomes
zero.

questions.question: Torque is defined as the cross product of position vector r and force F. If F is applied parallel to r, the torque is:
questions.explanation:
Torque equals rF sin θ. If force acts parallel to the position vector, θ = 0°, so torque
becomes zero.

questions.question: The value of i · (j × k) is:
questions.explanation: j × k = i and i · i = 1.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of the scalar product?
questions.explanation: The scalar product is commutative, so saying it is non-commutative is incorrect.

questions.question: If A = 2i + 3j and B = −2i − 3j, the angle between them is:
questions.explanation: Vector B is the negative of vector A, so the angle between them is 180°.

questions.question: The area of a parallelogram formed by two adjacent vectors A and B is equal to:
questions.explanation:
The magnitude of the cross product gives the area of the parallelogram formed by the two
vectors.

questions.question: If a force F of magnitude 10 N acts along the y-axis, its x-component is:
questions.explanation: A force acting entirely along the y-axis has no x-component.

questions.question: The vector product is anti-commutative, which means:
questions.explanation:
The cross product is anti-commutative:
A × B = −(B × A)

questions.question: Rectangular components of a vector are:

options.C: Always greater than the vector magnitude

questions.explanation: Rectangular components are always perpendicular to each other.

questions.question: If A · B = 0 and A × B = 0, then:

options.C: At least one of the vectors is a null vector

questions.explanation:
A · B = 0 means perpendicular vectors, while A × B = 0 means parallel vectors. This is
only possible if one vector is a null vector.

questions.question: For a vector A making an angle θ with the horizontal, if the vertical component is equal to the vector’s magnitude, then θ is:
questions.explanation: If the vertical component equals the magnitude, then sin θ = 1, giving θ = 90°.

questions.question: The scalar product of two mutually perpendicular vectors is:
questions.explanation: The dot product of perpendicular vectors is zero.

questions.question: Which physical quantity is an example of a scalar product?
questions.explanation:
Electric flux is a scalar quantity obtained from the dot product of electric field and area
vectors.

questions.question: The magnitude of the vector r = 3i − 4j is:
If n̂ is a unit vector perpendicular to both A and B, then A × B is:
questions.explanation:
The cross product equals AB sin θ multiplied by a unit vector perpendicular to both
vectors.

questions.question: Three vectors satisfy the relation A + B + C = 0. These vectors can form:
questions.explanation: If A + B + C = 0, the vectors can form a closed triangle.

questions.question: The direction of the vector product of two vectors is determined by:
questions.explanation: The direction of a vector product is determined by the Right Hand Rule.

questions.question: If A × B points along the positive z-axis, and A is along the positive x-axis, then B lies in the:
questions.explanation: Using the Right Hand Rule, B must lie along the positive y-direction.

questions.question: The unit vector along the direction of vector A is given by:
questions.explanation: A unit vector is obtained by dividing the vector by its magnitude.

questions.question: If the angle between two vectors is obtuse (90° < θ < 180°), their dot product is:
questions.explanation: For an obtuse angle, cos θ is negative, so the dot product is negative.

questions.question: j × k = ?
questions.explanation: j × k = i according to the cyclic order of unit vectors.

questions.question: A vector remains unchanged if:

options.A: It is rotated through an arbitrary angle
options.B: It is multiplied by a scalar
options.C: It is displaced parallel to itself
options.D: Its cross product is taken with a unit vector

questions.explanation: A vector remains unchanged if displaced parallel to itself.

questions.question: The component of vector A along the y-axis is found using:

options.A: A cos θ (if θ is with x-axis)
options.B: A sin θ (if θ is with x-axis)

questions.explanation: The y-component is A sin θ when θ is measured from the x-axis.

questions.question: Which pair of operations is not commutative?
questions.explanation: Both subtraction and vector product are non-commutative operations.

questions.question: If A = B, which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: If A = B, then the angle between them is 0°, so the cross product is zero.

questions.question: The square of the magnitude of a vector A is equal to:
questions.explanation: The square of the magnitude of a vector equals A · A.

questions.question: Given F = (2, 3) N and d = (4, 1) m, the work done is:
The scalar product of i and j is:
questions.explanation: The dot product of perpendicular unit vectors i and j is zero.

questions.question: If the scalar product of two vectors is equal to the product of their magnitudes, the angle between them is:
questions.explanation: If A · B = AB, then cos θ = 1 and θ = 0°.

questions.question: Angular momentum L is given by r × p. The direction of L is perpendicular to:
questions.explanation: Angular momentum is perpendicular to both position vector and momentum vector.

questions.question: What is the angle between i + j and i?
questions.explanation: The angle between i + j and i is 45°.

questions.question: k × i is equal to:
questions.explanation: k × i = j.

questions.question: The magnitude of the resultant of two forces 3 N and 4 N acting at right angles is:
questions.explanation: Resultant = √(3² + 4²) = 5 N.

questions.question: The position vector of a point P(a, b) is:
questions.explanation: The position vector of point (a, b) is ai + bj.

questions.question: If A × B = C, then C · A is:
questions.explanation: A × B is perpendicular to A, so their dot product is zero.

questions.question: At what angle is the x-component of a vector equal to its y-component?
questions.explanation: Equal x and y components mean tan θ = 1, therefore θ = 45°.

questions.question: The commutative property holds for:
questions.explanation: The commutative property applies only to the dot product.

questions.question: If the magnitude of the cross product of two vectors is √3 times their dot product, the angle is:
questions.explanation: If |A × B| = √3(A · B), then tan θ = √3, giving θ = 60°.

questions.question: A vector A has components Ax = −5 and Ay = −5. The direction of the vector is:
questions.explanation: Negative x and negative y components place the vector in the third quadrant at 225°.

questions.question: i · (i × j) is equal to:
questions.explanation: i × j = k and i · k = 0.

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Work is a scalar quantity.

questions.question: The cross product A × A yields:
questions.explanation: The cross product of a vector with itself is a null vector.

questions.question: In the expression P = F · v, if the angle between force and velocity is 90°, the power delivered is:
questions.explanation: Power = Fv cos θ. At 90°, cos 90° = 0.

questions.question: Which set of components could belong to a vector of magnitude 5?
questions.explanation: The components 3 and 4 give magnitude 5.

questions.question: The cross product of two vectors is a vector perpendicular to:
questions.explanation: The cross product is perpendicular to the plane containing the two vectors.

questions.question: A force of 50 N acts at 30° to the x-axis. The y-component is:
If A · B = −AB, then the angle between A and B is:
questions.explanation: If A · B = −AB, then cos θ = −1 and θ = 180°.

questions.question: The value of i × (j × k) is:
questions.explanation: j × k = i and i × i = 0.

questions.question: If vector A = 2i + j and B = i − j, then (A + B) · (A − B) is:
The projection of B on A is given by:
questions.explanation: Projection of B on A equals (A · B)/A.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding unit vectors?
questions.explanation: The dot product of a unit vector with itself equals 1.

questions.question: Two vectors are perpendicular if:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product.

questions.question: What is the magnitude of the vector product of A = 2i and B = 3j?
questions.explanation: (2i) × (3j) = 6k, whose magnitude is 6.

questions.question: The area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides represented by vectors A and B is given by:
questions.explanation: Area of a parallelogram equals |A × B|.

questions.question: If A = 3i + 4j, then the unit vector Â is:
questions.explanation: Magnitude of vector = 5, so the unit vector becomes 0.6i + 0.8j.

questions.question: The determinant form is used to calculate:
questions.explanation: The determinant method is used for calculating cross products in three dimensions.

questions.question: If the direction of A × B is along +k, then the direction of B × A is along:
questions.explanation: Reversing the order of cross product changes the direction.

questions.question: Which of the following operations results in a vector?
questions.explanation: A scalar multiplied by a vector gives another vector.

questions.question: i · (j × i) is:
questions.explanation: j × i = −k and i · (−k) = 0.

questions.question: If A and B are non-zero vectors and |A + B| = |A − B|, then the angle between them is:
questions.explanation: If |A + B| = |A − B|, then A · B = 0, meaning vectors are perpendicular.

questions.question: A vector having zero magnitude and arbitrary direction is called:
questions.explanation: A null vector has zero magnitude.

questions.question: The vector A has magnitude 10 and direction 60° with x-axis. Its y-component is:
(A × B) · A is always:
questions.explanation: (A × B) is perpendicular to A, so their dot product is zero.

questions.question: Which statement is true for the cross product of unit vectors?
questions.explanation: According to the right-hand rule, i × j = k.
